$comment: Publish options for azure.datafactory.tools, per environment.
This file uses a schema WE define; scripts/Deploy-DataFactory.ps1 reads it and
translates it into the module's own New-AdfPublishOption object. It is not a
file format the module reads directly - keeping the translation in our script
means an upstream option rename is a one-line fix here rather than a rewrite
of three workflow files.
Option semantics (see docs/06-data-factory.md for the long version):
excludes          Artefacts NOT to publish. Wildcards allowed. Format is
'<type>.<name>' or just '<type>.*'.
includes          If non-empty, ONLY these are published. Use for a targeted
hotfix deployment; leave empty for normal runs.
deleteNotInSource Remove artefacts present in the factory but absent from the
repository. This is what makes the factory converge on the
repo rather than accumulating orphans forever.
stopStartTriggers Stop every trigger before publishing and restart the ones
that should be running afterwards. Mandatory: ADF refuses
to modify a pipeline referenced by a STARTED trigger.
createNewInstance Create the factory if missing. Always false here - Terraform
owns factory creation, and a pipeline that can create
factories can create them in the wrong subscription.
deployGlobalParams Publish factory/*.json global parameters.
ignoreLogsAtEnd   Suppress the module's end-of-run log dump in CI.

dev.$comment: Dev is the Git-connected factory. deleteNotInSource stays TRUE so that an artefact deleted in a PR actually disappears from dev - otherwise dev slowly diverges from the repo and stops being a valid rehearsal for test.

prod.$comment: Identical to test on purpose. A different publish option between test and prod means test is not rehearsing prod. Protection in prod comes from the GitHub Environment approval gate, not from weakening the deployment.
